title: Sanitize project id to block path traversal in index file paths
description: create_project accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied id (the MCP create_project tool passes args.id straight through) and never validates it. project::delete builds filesystem paths with format!("{id}...") joined onto data_dir/indices, so an id like '../../Users/victim/file' escapes the directory: delete creates '{id}.mutation.lock' at an arbitrary path (OpenOptions create+write) and removes '{id}.tvim'/'{id}.uidmap.json' wherever such files exist. The MCP server is driven by LLM agents, so a prompt-injected agent gains an arbitrary file-create/delete primitive outside the data dir.
evidence:
let id = input.id.unwrap_or_else(|| slugify(&input.name));  // no validation
...
.join(format!("{id}.mutation.lock")),
suggestion: Validate ids against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ in project::create (and defensively in delete/get), or key filenames off the numeric rowid.

title: Stop sending JSON-RPC responses to notification messages
description: dispatch() answers every inbound message including notifications (messages without id). 'notifications/initialized' returns json!({}) — not even a valid JSON-RPC object — and every other notification falls into the catch-all arm emitting a -32601 error response with id null. JSON-RPC 2.0 forbids replying to notifications; strict clients can error or mis-correlate replies.
evidence:
"notifications/initialized" => json!({}),
_ => json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "error": { "code": -32601, ... } })
suggestion: When req.id.is_none(), do not write any response: handle known notifications explicitly and drop unknown ones silently.

title: Run blocking tools off the sequential dispatch loop
description: The stdio loop awaits dispatch() inline, so requests are strictly serialized. Heavy synchronous tools (ingest_project, consolidate, import_folder, export_memories) execute directly on the async task. While one large ingest runs, the server cannot answer ping, operation_status, or cancel_operation: wire-level cancellation of long operations is impossible and client timeouts fire.
evidence:
let response = match serde_json::from_str::<JsonRpcRequest>(trimmed) {
    Ok(req) => dispatch(&state, req).await,
suggestion: Spawn each request as a tokio task (JSON-RPC allows out-of-order responses) or run blocking tools via tokio::task::spawn_blocking; serialize stdout writes behind a mutex.

title: Disable the file watcher when deleting a project
description: project::delete removes memories, the project row, and index files, but never calls io::disable_watch and never removes the WATCHERS registry entry. A deleted-but-watched project keeps its notify watcher alive: every filesystem event re-triggers a watch ingest that fails at project::get, spamming errors; if a new project is later created with the same id, the stale watcher silently ingests the OLD root_path into the NEW project.
evidence:
// delete body only: flush_all_indices / indices.write().remove / remove_file / db.write(DELETE...)
// io.rs:205: WATCHERS.write().remove(project_id);  <- only inside disable_watch
suggestion: Call crate::io::disable_watch(state, id) inside project::delete before dropping the rows.

title: Add a single-instance guard for the desktop app
description: run() registers no single-instance plugin (tauri-plugin-single-instance absent from Cargo.toml). Launching biTurbo twice yields two full AppState processes over the same SQLite DB and indices dir: duplicate tray icons, two consolidate schedulers, two debounced index flushers rewriting the same .tvim files where last-writer-wins loses vectors.
evidence:
.plugin(tauri_plugin_autostart::Builder::new().build())
.plugin(tauri_plugin_shell::init())
... // no single-instance plugin
suggestion: Add tauri-plugin-single-instance as the first plugin, focusing the existing window on second launch.

title: Clamp the list tool limit to prevent unbounded queries
description: The list handler passes limit raw into memory::list which interpolates it as i64 into SQL LIMIT with no clamp. limit=9223372036854775808 wraps to i64::MIN; SQLite treats negative LIMIT as no limit, serializing the entire memories table into one JSON response (memory spike, hung connection).
evidence: let limit = args.get("limit").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(50) as usize;
suggestion: Clamp in the handler (limit.clamp(1, 500), mirroring bounded_k) or clamp inside memory::list.

title: Spawn scheduler in the standalone MCP binary or hide consolidate_status
description: The GUI spawns the consolidate scheduler (lib.rs:105) but the standalone MCP binary never does, while still exposing consolidate_status. In MCP-only sessions the tool reports idle/never-run forever and background decay/dedup never happens unless the agent manually calls consolidate.
evidence: run_mcp_server_stdio().await   // no scheduler::spawn anywhere in main
suggestion: Spawn the scheduler on the opened AppState inside run_mcp_server_stdio, or document consolidate_status as GUI-only.

title: Validate submit_recall_feedback value instead of defaulting and wrapping
description: value defaults a missing/invalid value to +1 (unwrap_or(1)), silently recording positive feedback. Additionally `as i8` truncates: 256 becomes 0, 300 becomes 44, 1000 becomes -24 — out-of-range values flip or zero the feedback signal instead of being rejected, corrupting recall ranking.
evidence: let value = args.get("value").and_then(|v| v.as_i64()).unwrap_or(1) as i8;
suggestion: Return Invalid when value missing; accept only -1 or 1.

title: Reject agent names that slugify to an empty id
description: register_agent derives the primary key via slugify(name), which maps every non-alphanumeric-ASCII char to '-' and drops empty parts. A non-ASCII name yields id "" — all such agents collapse into one upserted ghost row with empty id. Returned AgentEntry always reports created_at=now even when upserting an existing row.
evidence:
let id = slugify(&name);
Ok(AgentEntry { id, name, kind, last_seen: now, created_at: now, meta })
suggestion: Error on empty slug (fall back to uuid), read back actual created_at after upsert.

title: Verify explicit project_id exists in resolve_project_id
description: An explicitly supplied project_id is returned without existence check, unlike remember/ingest paths which validate via require_project. search/recall_for_context with a typo'd id then return empty results ('no relevant memories') instead of an error, leading agents to wrongly conclude the project has no memories.
suggestion: Run project::get(state, pid) for the explicit-id branch and propagate NotFound.

title: Make .biTurbo projectName resolution deterministic on name collisions
description: Resolution queries 'WHERE name = ?1 OR id = ?1 LIMIT 1'. Two projects can share a name; LIMIT 1 picks an arbitrary row and recall rooted at a directory whose .biTurbo says projectName=X can attach to the wrong project, surfacing another project's memories as context.
evidence: "SELECT id FROM projects WHERE name = ?1 OR id = ?1 LIMIT 1"
suggestion: Prefer exact id match; on multiple name matches return ambiguity error listing candidates.

title: Try-lock queued operations before resuming them in a second process
description: Both GUI and every MCP binary instance call operations::resume_pending on the shared data dir. resume_pending spawns executors for every 'queued' row without try-locking the per-operation lock; executors use blocking lock_exclusive. Two processes starting simultaneously both spawn a thread for the same queued op — second blocks then re-runs the entire operation after the first finishes (duplicate work, doubled activity records). recover_interrupted already models the correct try-lock-and-skip pattern.
evidence: spawn_ingest(state.clone(), operation.id, project_id, root);  // no try_lock
suggestion: try_lock the operation lock in resume_pending before spawning; skip ops already claimed by a live process.

title: Guard export_memories output_path against overwriting arbitrary files
description: The MCP export_memories tool writes JSON to any caller-supplied output_path: create_dir_all's parent and unconditionally fs::write's, clobbering existing files. Exposed to LLM agents, this is an arbitrary-file-overwrite primitive reachable via prompt injection.
suggestion: Refuse to overwrite existing file unless explicit overwrite flag passed; confine exports beneath app data dir.

title: Drop the discarded inline instructions literal in initialize
description: The initialize arm embeds a large hand-written instructions string then immediately overwrites response["result"]["instructions"] with MCP_INSTRUCTIONS. Dead weight and drift hazard (two instruction texts to keep in sync).
evidence:
let mut response = ok(&id, json!({ ... "instructions": "## biTurbo Memory Layer — Instructions\n\n..." }));
response["result"]["instructions"] = Value::String(MCP_INSTRUCTIONS.into());
suggestion: Build the result once from MCP_INSTRUCTIONS only.

title: Refresh tray stats immediately instead of after 30 seconds
description: The tray stats thread sleeps 30 seconds before its first query, so menu items show 'Memories: —' for up to half a minute after launch.
evidence:
.spawn(move || loop {
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(30));
suggestion: Run the refresh body once before entering the sleep loop.

title: Only hide the window on tray click when it is focused
description: toggle_main_window hides whenever is_visible() is true. A visible but unfocused window gets hidden by left-click instead of brought to front — opposite of toggle intent.
evidence:
match window.is_visible() {
    Ok(true) => { let _ = window.hide(); }
suggestion: Hide only when is_visible() && is_focused(); otherwise show and focus.

title: Send GUI tracing console output to stderr instead of stdout
description: init_logging attaches a tracing layer to std::io::stdout. Today MCP transport lives in a separate binary so protocol stream is safe — but any future in-process stdio use, or piping GUI stdout, interleaves log lines with data output. stderr is conventional for diagnostics.
evidence: .with_writer(std::io::stdout),
suggestion: Switch console layer to std::io::stderr.

title: Log resume_pending failures instead of discarding them
description: `let _ = operations::resume_pending(state_arc.clone());` discards the Result. If recovery fails (locked DB, IO error), queued operations silently never resume and nothing reaches logs.
evidence: let _ = operations::resume_pending(state_arc.clone());
suggestion: Match on error and tracing::error! it with context.

title: Fail gracefully at startup instead of panicking on expect
description: setup() uses expect() for app_data_dir and AppState::open, run() ends in expect(). A corrupted DB or unresolvable path makes the app crash-loop invisibly on macOS release builds (no console, no dialog), and no custom panic hook routes panics into the log file.
evidence:
let data_dir = app.path().app_data_dir().expect("app data dir resolvable");
let mut state = AppState::open(&data_dir).expect("open app state");
suggestion: Install a panic hook logging to file appender; convert startup failures into user-visible dialog / clean non-zero exit.

title: Preserve SQLite error codes in BiError::Db
description: From<rusqlite::Error> flattens to e.to_string(), discarding sqlite error code. Callers cannot programmatically distinguish UNIQUE violations from BUSY/READONLY, so surfaces emit raw strings and cannot map to friendly actionable messages.
suggestion: Carry e.sqlite_error_code()/extended code alongside message in Db variant.

title: Validate bit_width instead of truncating with as u8
description: create_project reads bit_width as u64 then casts with `as u8`: values above 255 wrap silently (300 becomes 44) and unsupported widths flow unchecked into index quantization config, producing confusing downstream behavior instead of clear input error.
evidence: bit_width: args.get("bit_width").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).map(|n| n as u8),
suggestion: Use u8::try_from(n).ok() and validate against supported bit-width allowlist.

title: Surface .biTurbo marker write failures in create_project
description: After inserting the project row, failure to write the .biTurbo marker swallowed with `let _ =`. If root_path doesn't exist or isn't writable, project created without marker and later root_path-based resolution silently falls back to default project — hard-to-diagnose isolation breakage. create also never checks root_path exists, unlike ensure_marker_files.
suggestion: Propagate write error (or log) and validate root_path.is_dir() at create time.

title: Purge recall_feedback rows when deleting a project
description: delete removes memories and project row but leaves recall_feedback rows whose memory_uid belonged to deleted memories. Orphaned feedback accumulates unboundedly across project lifecycles keeping stale ranking signals.
evidence:
tx.execute("DELETE FROM memories WHERE project_id = ?1", ...)?;
tx.execute("DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?1", ...)?;
suggestion: Delete feedback for the project's uids within same transaction.

title: Support or cleanly reject JSON-RPC batch requests
description: A top-level JSON array (JSON-RPC batch, permitted by MCP 2024-11-05 revision advertised) fails deserialization into JsonRpcRequest and is answered with single -32700 parse error instead of per-entry responses.
suggestion: Deserialize to Value; on Array dispatch each element and reply with array — or explicitly reject batches with -32600.

title: Fail loudly when SCHEMAS_JSON drifts from implemented tools
description: tool_schemas() silently degrades to empty tools list if embedded JSON fails to parse — every client would see zero tools. Additionally 7 implemented handlers absent from SCHEMAS_JSON (intentional per 27-tool note) but nothing asserts advertised set matches dispatcher, so future drift invisible.
suggestion: Panic or log error on schema parse failure; add unit test asserting every advertised tool has a call_tool arm.

title: De-flake smoke tests: model dependency and fixed 3s windows
description: Every smoke test opens full AppState (fastembed BGE embedder) and polls filesystem with fixed 200ms sleeps inside 3-second deadlines. On cold machine model must be present/downloaded before search works; on slow CI the 3s window can elapse before debounced flusher fires — flaky failures unrelated to regressions.
suggestion: Use stub/deterministic embedder for tests or derive completion from observable flush events; make timeouts generous/configurable.

title: Share one app-identifier constant between MCP server and GUI
description: run_mcp_server_stdio hardcodes dirs::data_dir().join("com.biturbo.app"), duplicating identifier from tauri.conf.json. If bundle identifier ever changes, GUI and MCP server silently operate on different datasets.
suggestion: Export pub const APP_IDENTIFIER from biturbo_lib and use in both.

title: Do not fall back to CWD for the data dir in the MCP binary
description: dirs::data_dir().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(".")) makes the binary open/create com.biturbo.app under whatever directory the agent launched it from when OS data dir unavailable — silently splitting state and scattering logs into unrelated working directories.
suggestion: Exit with clear error when OS data dir cannot be determined instead of falling back to '.'.
